newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.

text.p: BELL ADVISED TO STAY PUT
The lawyer for alleged paedophile, Phillip Bell, says he's advising his client to remain in South Africa and fight attempts to extradite him to Australia.
The former Sydney businessman, now facing more than two hundred warrants alleging child sexual assault in Australia, was arrested last week in South Africa.
Mr Bell's lawyer, Jim Boyens says South Africa enacted new extradition laws to enable police to arrest his client and ensure his return to Australia.
Mr Boyens says Mr Bell will fight attempts to extradite him because he feels he's been made a victim of his lifestyle.
Mr Bell is due in Court later today.
THE PUSH CONTINUES FOR UNITED APPROACH ON NATIVE TITLE
Victorian Premier Jeff Kennett says he's hopeful the Prime Minister will agree to a national approach to the native title issue.
Mr Kennett and his Queensland and West Australian counterparts agreement to a speedy meeting with John Howard is essential to determine the future of native title.
All three are pushing for clarification of the Wik claim, saying it has different implications within in each state and territory.
The High Court's Wik ruling decrees that native title and pastoral leases can co-exist.
Meanwhile a senior figure in the Anglican Church says the Wik decision should be an example of how all people can deal with each other and the environment.
The Bishop of Canberra and Goulburn says governments should look at the example set by some mining companies which co-exist with Aboriginal interests.
VEST PLAN LABELLED SILLY
The Council for Civil Liberties has branded a Northern Territory plan to make people convicted of minor offences wear fluorescent vests, a silly public relations stunt.
The Territory Government has announced people serving community service orders will have to wear bright orange bibs with "community service".
Territory Correctional Services Minister Steve Hatton says the vests will enable members of the public to see where community service orders are being carried out.
But civil libertarian Terry O'Gorman says the move shows just how out of control the law and order debate has become..and only serves to cheapen the criminal justice system.
EUTHANASIA COMMITTEE IN NT
The Senate Committee investigating the issue of voluntary euthanasia will be in the Northern Territory this week.
The Committee, which is due to report to the Senate next month prior to the vote on the Kevin Andrews anti-euthanasia bill, will hold public hearings in Darwin on Friday.
Committee member, Territory Senator, Bob Collins says an evening forum on Thursday will be open to anyone who wants to express a view about voluntary euthanasia.
NEW RADAR SYSTEM FOR ARMY
The Australian Army's air defence regiment is to get radar systems and night vision devices for its portable ground-to-air guided missiles.
Defence minister, Ian McLachlan, says British Aerospace Australia will supply the radar systems, expected to be in use with the regiment at Woodside in South Australia by late next year.
He says clip-on night devices have already been bought under a separate contract with Bofors Australia, and should go into service early next year.
Together, the additions will enable the regiment's RBS-70 missiles to be used around-the-clock.
Soldiers from the regiment went on Australian warships, to improve their defences, when they were sent to the Gulf War in 1991.
GUN BATTLE HAS SEQUEL IN COURT
In far north Queensland, six men are due to appear before the city's Magistrates court this morning charged over a gun battle on a suburban street on Saturday.

Although no-one was hurt in the incident, residents in a Cairns suburb were forced to seek shelter after shots were fired at a home which police believe was occupied by bikies belonging to the Renegades motorcycle club.
Police suspect the shots were fired as members of the Gypsy Jokers club drove by the house on Saturday afternoon.
MINISTER COMMITTED TO RESORT'S ENVIRONMENTAL GUIDELINES
The Federal Environment Minister's office says it's satisfied that development at the Port Hinchinbrook site in North Queensland is meeting current environmental guidelines.
The Environment Minister, Robert Hill expressed concerns late last year over two issues of the deed of agreement which he believed were in danger of being breached.
However, a spokesman for the minister says those concerns - the lack of a site supervisor and problems with turbidity - have been addressed by the developer.
He says the minister is 100 percent committed to making sure all environmental guidelines are followed.
